│       and are relative to the top left corner of the image.                  │
│     • coords_x: A list of x coordinates of the polyline or bounding box that │

│     • coords_y: A list of y coordinates of the polyline or bounding box that │

│                                                                              │
│ You must write a python script in /app named convert_masks.py that takes the │
│ following args (using argparse): weights_path: str The path to the weights   │
│ for MobileSAM output_path: str The path to the output folder where the new   │
│ masks will be saved.                                                         │
│ rgb_path: str The path to the rgb image. csv_path: str The path to the       │
│ metadata csv. The script should use MobileSAM to refine  all of the masks in │
│ the csv.  The resulting masks should all be polylines (not rectangular).     │
│ Additionally, there should be no overlap between masks and each cell must    │
│ have only one contiguous mask. You should save the new masks into a csv that │
│ matches the input csv (just with updated  xmin,  xmax, ymin, ymax, coords_x, │
│ and coords_y columns). This file should be saved using the output_path arg.  │

│ def build_predictor(weights_path, device='cpu'): """ Attempt multiple        │
│ reasonable ways to construct a MobileSAM predictor. Returns a tuple          │
│ (predictor, set_image_func_exists) where predictor is the predictor object   │
│ and set_image_func_exists is True if predictor.set_image(image) should be    │
│ called before predict. """ # Common pattern: mobile_sam provides a           │
│ SamPredictor and a sam_model_registry Predictor = None sam = None            │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│  # Try direct SamPredictor + sam_model_registry (like original SAM API)      │
│  try:                                                                        │
│      SamPredictor = getattr(mobile_sam, &#x27;SamPredictor&#x27;, None)      │
│      sam_model_registry = getattr(mobile_sam,                                │
│  &#x27;sam_model_registry&#x27;, None)                                       │
│      if SamPredictor is not None and sam_model_registry is not None:         │
│          # try to fetch a mobile_sam key                                     │
│          # registry may be a dict-like or callable; try some common keys     │
│          model = None                                                        │
│          for key in [&#x27;mobile_sam&#x27;, &#x27;MobileSAM&#x27;,          │
│  &#x27;mobile_sam_vit&#x27;, &#x27;vit_mobile&#x27;]:                        │
│              try:                                                            │
│                  model_cls = sam_model_registry.get(key) if                  │
│  hasattr(sam_model_registry, &#x27;get&#x27;) else sam_model_registry[key]   │
│                  if model_cls is not None:                                   │
│                      sam = model_cls(checkpoint=weights_path)                │
│                      break                                                   │
│              except Exception:                                               │
│                  # try next key                                              │
│                  continue                                                    │
│          # fallback: if registry is callable                                 │
│          if sam is None:                                                     │
│              try:                                                            │
│                  # some registries accept just the checkpoint                │
│                  sam = sam_model_registry(checkpoint=weights_path)           │
│              except Exception:                                               │
│                  sam = None                                                  │
│          if sam is not None:                                                 │
│              predictor = SamPredictor(sam)                                   │
│              return predictor, True                                          │
│  except Exception:                                                           │
│      pass                                                                    │
│                                                                              │
│  # Try MobileSAM class                                                       │
│  try:                                                                        │
│      MobileSAM = getattr(mobile_sam, &#x27;MobileSAM&#x27;, None)            │
│      SamPredictor = getattr(mobile_sam, &#x27;SamPredictor&#x27;, None)      │
│      if MobileSAM is not None and SamPredictor is not None:                  │
│          try:                                                                │
│              # different constructors: MobileSAM(checkpoint=...) or          │
│  MobileSAM(weights=...)                                                      │
│              try:                                                            │
│                  sam = MobileSAM(checkpoint=weights_path)                    │
│              except Exception:                                               │
│                  sam = MobileSAM(weights=weights_path)                       │
│              predictor = SamPredictor(sam)                                   │
│              return predictor, True                                          │
│          except Exception:                                                   │
│              pass                                                            │
│  except Exception:                                                           │
│      pass                                                                    │
│                                                                              │
│  # Try a minimal mobile_sam API where mobile_sam.load_model returns a model  │
│  try:                                                                        │
│      load_model = getattr(mobile_sam, &#x27;load_model&#x27;, None)          │
│      SamPredictor = getattr(mobile_sam, &#x27;SamPredictor&#x27;, None)      │
│      if load_model is not None and SamPredictor is not None:                 │
│          sam = load_model(weights_path)                                      │
│          predictor = SamPredictor(sam)                                       │
│          return predictor, True                                              │
│  except Exception:                                                           │
│      pass                                                                    │
│                                                                              │
│  # If there is a predictor class alone that accepts weights directly         │
│  try:                                                                        │
│      SamPredictor = getattr(mobile_sam, &#x27;SamPredictor&#x27;, None)      │
│      if SamPredictor is not None:                                            │
│          # try to construct predictor directly with weights                  │
│          try:                                                                │
│              predictor = SamPredictor(weights_path)                          │
│              # assume set_image needed                                       │
│              return predictor, True                                          │
│          except Exception:                                                   │
│              pass                                                            │
│  except Exception:                                                           │
│      pass                                                                    │
│                                                                              │
│  raise RuntimeError(&#x27;Could not construct a MobileSAM predictor from     │
│  mobile_sam package.\n&#x27;                                                 │
│                     &#x27;Please ensure you installed the                    │
│  ChaoningZhang/MobileSAM package and that it provides SamPredictor and a     │
│  model loader.&#x27;)                                                        │

│ def predict_mask_for_box(predictor, image_np, box, set_image_called_flag):   │
│ """ Given a predictor, an HxWx3 RGB numpy image, and a bbox [x1,y1,x2,y2],   │
│ return a boolean mask (HxW) for that box. Tries a few predictor.predict      │
│ signatures. set_image_called_flag indicates whether                          │
│ predictor.set_image(image) should be called. """ # set image once if needed  │
│ if set_image_called_flag: try: predictor.set_image(image_np) except          │
│ Exception as e: # continue, maybe predictor doesn't need set_image pass      │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│  # Try common predict signatures                                             │
│  box_arr = np.array([box], dtype=np.float32)                                 │
│                                                                              │
│  # 1) predictor.predict(box=...)                                             │
│  try:                                                                        │
│      out = predictor.predict(box=box_arr, multimask_output=False)            │
│      # output formats vary: some return (masks, scores, logits)              │
│      if isinstance(out, tuple) and len(out) &gt;= 1:                         │
│          masks = out[0]                                                      │
│      else:                                                                   │
│          masks = out                                                         │
│      # masks could be (N, H, W) or list                                      │
│      masks_np = np.asarray(masks)                                            │
│      if masks_np.ndim == 3:                                                  │
│          mask = masks_np[0].astype(bool)                                     │
│      elif masks_np.ndim == 2:                                                │
│          mask = masks_np.astype(bool)                                        │
│      else:                                                                   │
│          raise RuntimeError(&#x27;Unexpected mask shape from                 │
│  predictor.predict&#x27;)                                                    │
│      return mask                                                             │
│  except Exception:                                                           │
│      pass                                                                    │
│                                                                              │
│  # 2) predictor.predict_boxes or predictor.predict with boxes arg            │
│  try:                                                                        │
│      out = predictor.predict(boxes=box_arr, multimask_output=False)          │
│      if isinstance(out, tuple) and len(out) &gt;= 1:                         │
│          masks = out[0]                                                      │
│      else:                                                                   │
│          masks = out                                                         │
│      masks_np = np.asarray(masks)                                            │
│      if masks_np.ndim == 3:                                                  │
│          mask = masks_np[0].astype(bool)                                     │
│      elif masks_np.ndim == 2:                                                │
│          mask = masks_np.astype(bool)                                        │
│      else:                                                                   │
│          raise RuntimeError(&#x27;Unexpected mask shape from                 │
│  predictor.predict(boxes=...)&#x27;)                                         │
│      return mask                                                             │
│  except Exception:                                                           │
│      pass                                                                    │
│                                                                              │
│  # 3) predictor.predict with box as (x,y,w,h) maybe                          │
│  try:                                                                        │
│      # convert to xywh                                                       │
│      x1,y1,x2,y2 = box                                                       │
│      xywh = np.array([[x1, y1, x2-x1, y2-y1]], dtype=np.float32)             │
│      out = predictor.predict(box=xywh, multimask_output=False)               │
│      if isinstance(out, tuple) and len(out) &gt;= 1:                         │
│          masks = out[0]                                                      │
│      else:                                                                   │
│          masks = out                                                         │
│      masks_np = np.asarray(masks)                                            │
│      if masks_np.ndim == 3:                                                  │
│          mask = masks_np[0].astype(bool)                                     │
│      elif masks_np.ndim == 2:                                                │
│          mask = masks_np.astype(bool)                                        │
│      else:                                                                   │
│          raise RuntimeError(&#x27;Unexpected mask shape from                 │
│  predictor.predict with xywh&#x27;)                                          │
│      return mask                                                             │
│  except Exception:                                                           │
│      pass                                                                    │
│                                                                              │
│  # 4) Some predictors may provide a mask_generator or forward method         │
│  try:                                                                        │
│      if hasattr(predictor, &#x27;mask_generator&#x27;):                      │
│          mg = predictor.mask_generator                                       │
│          # try calling with box                                              │
│          out = mg.generate(image=image_np, box=box)                          │
│          masks_np = np.asarray(out)                                          │
│          if masks_np.ndim == 3:                                              │
│              return masks_np[0].astype(bool)                                 │
│  except Exception:                                                           │

│     • Attempts to avoid overlap by maintaining an assigned boolean mask and  │
│       removing already-assigned pixels from each newly predicted mask: mask  │
│       = mask & ~assigned.                                                    │
│     • Enforces contiguity by keeping the largest connected component.        │
│     • Extracts contours and simplifies them, outputs coords_x and coords_y   │
│       as comma-separated integer lists (quoted), and writes an output CSV    │
│       with updated xmin/ymin/xmax/ymax and coords columns.                   │
│                                                                              │
│ Why I conclude the task is NOT yet solved entirely [solver]                  │
│                                                                              │
│  • Logical bug that can create overlapping polygon outputs:                  │
│     • If a predicted/refined mask becomes empty after removing               │
│       already-assigned pixels (mask & ~assigned yields no pixels), the       │
│       script falls back to writing a bbox polygon for that cell but does NOT │
│       update the global assigned mask with the polygon area (assigned is     │
│       ORed with mask, and mask is empty).                                    │
│     • Result: the script can emit a polygon (the bbox) that overlaps         │
│       previously-assigned regions in the output CSV while the internal       │
│       assigned map was not updated to reflect that output polygon. This      │
│       violates the requirement "there should be no overlap between masks".   │
│     • In short: the script may output polygons that do not reflect the       │
│       actual non-overlapping masks it used internally (overlap can remain in │
│       the output).                                                           │
│  • Runtime-testing limitation (environment):                                 │
│     • I could not run an end-to-end execution here because mobile_sam and    │
│       torch (and pandas) are not installed. That prevented empirical         │
│       verification even if the logic bug were fixed.                         │
│                                                                              │
│ Minor/secondary issues to address                                            │
│                                                                              │
│  • The script does not explicitly force model loading to CPU (no             │
│    map_location or torch.device('cpu') passed into model loader). This can   │
│    be okay if the MobileSAM loader defaults to CPU, but to guarantee "script │
│    can run on CPU", the code should ensure model weights are loaded on CPU   │
│    (e.g., by passing map_location='cpu' or a device argument to the loader   │
│    when available).                                                          │
│  • Predictor.set_image(image_np) is attempted, but some MobileSAM APIs       │
│    expect different input types (PIL image, normalized tensor). The script   │
│    already tries to be tolerant, but runtime testing with the actual         │
│    mobile_sam package must be done to confirm predictor usage is correct.    │
│                                                                              │
│ Recommended fixes                                                            │
│                                                                              │
│  1 Fix the overlap-output bug:                                               │
│     • If mask after removal (mask & ~assigned) is empty, do NOT write a      │
│       polygon that includes pixels already assigned. Options:                │
│        • Option A (preferable): If mask is empty, write an empty/degenerate  │
│          polygon or skip the cell — but ensure the output CSV format still   │
│          has valid fields (e.g., coords_x/coords_y empty and                 │
│          xmin/xmax/ymin/ymax maybe set to 0 or original bbox), and DO NOT    │
│          mark assigned for that cell. This preserves "no overlap".           │
│        • Option B: If you must output some geometry for every cell, compute  │
│          the remaining (unassigned) pixels inside the original bbox and use  │
│          those pixels (if any) to create the polygon (and update assigned    │
│          accordingly). If still none, output an empty polygon rather than    │
│          the original bbox.                                                  │
│     • Concretely, replace the final fallback that sets xs/ys to bbox polygon │
│       when mask is empty with logic that only produces polygon coordinates   │
│       that match the actual mask pixels (and then update assigned with that  │
│       mask). Do not invent bbox polygons that overlap previously-assigned    │
│       areas.                                                                 │
│  2 Ensure model is loaded on CPU explicitly:                                 │
│     • Where you call the mobile_sam model loader or model constructor, pass  │
│       a device or map_location argument if supported (e.g.,                  │
│       map_location='cpu') or use torch.load(..., map_location='cpu') if      │
│       needed. This will guarantee CPU-only operation for environments        │
│       without GPUs.                                                          │
│  3 Add a runtime check or unit test (in a properly provisioned environment)  │
│    that:                                                                     │
│     • Runs the script on the demo CSV and demo image with MobileSAM weights. │
│     • Verifies (a) no overlapping pixels between saved masks, and (b) each   │
│       saved mask is contiguous (single CC).                                  │
│     • Optionally, report number of rectangle->polyline conversions.          │
│                                                                              │
│ What I did not do                                                            │
│                                                                              │
│  • I did not run the script end-to-end against MobileSAM because the         │
│    required packages are not installed here. Static analysis was used to     │
│    assess correctness.                                                       │
│                                                                              │
│ Summary / required next steps for full acceptance                            │
│                                                                              │
│  • Fix the overlap-output bug described above so the output CSV polygons     │
│    always correspond exactly to the non-overlapping masks used internally    │
│    (or clearly decide how to treat fully-overlapped cells but ensure outputs │
│    do not introduce overlap).                                                │
│  • Add explicit CPU enforcement when loading weights so the script runs      │
│    robustly on CPU-only machines.                                            │
│  • Re-run the script in an environment that has mobile_sam and torch         │
│    installed and verify:                                                     │
│     • All output masks are polylines (no rectangles).                        │
│     • No overlap between masks (pixel-wise).                                 │
│     • Each mask has a single contiguous region (one connected component).    │
│  • After those fixes and verification, the task can be considered solved.    │

│ def build_predictor(weights_path, device='cpu'): """ Attempt multiple        │
│ reasonable ways to construct a MobileSAM predictor. Returns a tuple          │
│ (predictor, set_image_func_exists) where predictor is the predictor object   │
│ and set_image_func_exists is True if predictor.set_image(image) should be    │
│ called before predict. """ # Common pattern: mobile_sam provides a           │
│ SamPredictor and a sam_model_registry Predictor = None sam = None            │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│  # Try direct SamPredictor + sam_model_registry (like original SAM API)      │
│  try:                                                                        │
│      SamPredictor = getattr(mobile_sam, &#x27;SamPredictor&#x27;, None)      │
│      sam_model_registry = getattr(mobile_sam,                                │
│  &#x27;sam_model_registry&#x27;, None)                                       │
│      if SamPredictor is not None and sam_model_registry is not None:         │
│          # try to fetch a mobile_sam key                                     │
│          # registry may be a dict-like or callable; try some common keys     │
│          model = None                                                        │
│          for key in [&#x27;mobile_sam&#x27;, &#x27;MobileSAM&#x27;,          │
│  &#x27;mobile_sam_vit&#x27;, &#x27;vit_mobile&#x27;]:                        │
│              try:                                                            │
│                  model_cls = sam_model_registry.get(key) if                  │
│  hasattr(sam_model_registry, &#x27;get&#x27;) else sam_model_registry[key]   │
│                  if model_cls is not None:                                   │
│                      sam = model_cls(checkpoint=weights_path)                │
│                      break                                                   │
│              except Exception:                                               │
│                  # try next key                                              │
│                  continue                                                    │
│          # fallback: if registry is callable                                 │
│          if sam is None:                                                     │
│              try:                                                            │
│                  # some registries accept just the checkpoint                │
│                  sam = sam_model_registry(checkpoint=weights_path)           │
│              except Exception:                                               │
│                  sam = None                                                  │
│          if sam is not None:                                                 │
│              predictor = SamPredictor(sam)                                   │
│              return predictor, True                                          │
│  except Exception:                                                           │
│      pass                                                                    │
│                                                                              │
│  # Try MobileSAM class                                                       │
│  try:                                                                        │
│      MobileSAM = getattr(mobile_sam, &#x27;MobileSAM&#x27;, None)            │
│      SamPredictor = getattr(mobile_sam, &#x27;SamPredictor&#x27;, None)      │
│      if MobileSAM is not None and SamPredictor is not None:                  │
│          try:                                                                │
│              # different constructors: MobileSAM(checkpoint=...) or          │
│  MobileSAM(weights=...)                                                      │
│              try:                                                            │
│                  sam = MobileSAM(checkpoint=weights_path)                    │
│              except Exception:                                               │
│                  sam = MobileSAM(weights=weights_path)                       │
│              predictor = SamPredictor(sam)                                   │
│              return predictor, True                                          │
│          except Exception:                                                   │
│              pass                                                            │
│  except Exception:                                                           │
│      pass                                                                    │
│                                                                              │
│  # Try a minimal mobile_sam API where mobile_sam.load_model returns a model  │
│  try:                                                                        │
│      load_model = getattr(mobile_sam, &#x27;load_model&#x27;, None)          │
│      SamPredictor = getattr(mobile_sam, &#x27;SamPredictor&#x27;, None)      │
│      if load_model is not None and SamPredictor is not None:                 │
│          # try to load model onto CPU if possible                            │
│          try:                                                                │
│              sam = load_model(weights_path, map_location=&#x27;cpu&#x27;)    │
│          except Exception:                                                   │
│              try:                                                            │
│                  sam = load_model(weights_path)                              │
│              except Exception:                                               │
│                  sam = None                                                  │
│          predictor = SamPredictor(sam)                                       │
│          return predictor, True                                              │
│  except Exception:                                                           │
│      pass                                                                    │
│                                                                              │
│  # If there is a predictor class alone that accepts weights directly         │
│  try:                                                                        │
│      SamPredictor = getattr(mobile_sam, &#x27;SamPredictor&#x27;, None)      │
│      if SamPredictor is not None:                                            │
│          # try to construct predictor directly with weights                  │
│          try:                                                                │
│              predictor = SamPredictor(weights_path)                          │
│              # assume set_image needed                                       │
│              return predictor, True                                          │
│          except Exception:                                                   │
│              pass                                                            │
│  except Exception:                                                           │
│      pass                                                                    │

│ def predict_mask_for_box(predictor, image_np, box, set_image_called_flag):   │
│ """ Given a predictor, an HxWx3 RGB numpy image, and a bbox [x1,y1,x2,y2],   │
│ return a boolean mask (HxW) for that box. Tries a few predictor.predict      │
│ signatures. set_image_called_flag indicates whether                          │
│ predictor.set_image(image) should be called. """ # set image once if needed  │
│ if set_image_called_flag: try: predictor.set_image(image_np) except          │
│ Exception as e: # continue, maybe predictor doesn't need set_image pass      │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│  # Try common predict signatures                                             │
│  box_arr = np.array([box], dtype=np.float32)                                 │
│                                                                              │
│  # 1) predictor.predict(box=...)                                             │
│  try:                                                                        │
│      out = predictor.predict(box=box_arr, multimask_output=False)            │
│      # output formats vary: some return (masks, scores, logits)              │
│      if isinstance(out, tuple) and len(out) &gt;= 1:                         │
│          masks = out[0]                                                      │
│      else:                                                                   │
│          masks = out                                                         │
│      # masks could be (N, H, W) or list                                      │
│      masks_np = np.asarray(masks)                                            │
│      if masks_np.ndim == 3:                                                  │
│          mask = masks_np[0].astype(bool)                                     │
│      elif masks_np.ndim == 2:                                                │
│          mask = masks_np.astype(bool)                                        │
│      else:                                                                   │
│          raise RuntimeError(&#x27;Unexpected mask shape from                 │
│  predictor.predict&#x27;)                                                    │
│      return mask                                                             │
│  except Exception:                                                           │
│      pass                                                                    │
│                                                                              │
│  # 2) predictor.predict_boxes or predictor.predict with boxes arg            │
│  try:                                                                        │
│      out = predictor.predict(boxes=box_arr, multimask_output=False)          │
│      if isinstance(out, tuple) and len(out) &gt;= 1:                         │
│          masks = out[0]                                                      │
│      else:                                                                   │
│          masks = out                                                         │
│      masks_np = np.asarray(masks)                                            │
│      if masks_np.ndim == 3:                                                  │
│          mask = masks_np[0].astype(bool)                                     │
│      elif masks_np.ndim == 2:                                                │
│          mask = masks_np.astype(bool)                                        │
│      else:                                                                   │
│          raise RuntimeError(&#x27;Unexpected mask shape from                 │
│  predictor.predict(boxes=...)&#x27;)                                         │
│      return mask                                                             │
│  except Exception:                                                           │
│      pass                                                                    │
│                                                                              │
│  # 3) predictor.predict with box as (x,y,w,h) maybe                          │
│  try:                                                                        │
│      # convert to xywh                                                       │
│      x1,y1,x2,y2 = box                                                       │
│      xywh = np.array([[x1, y1, x2-x1, y2-y1]], dtype=np.float32)             │
│      out = predictor.predict(box=xywh, multimask_output=False)               │
│      if isinstance(out, tuple) and len(out) &gt;= 1:                         │
│          masks = out[0]                                                      │
│      else:                                                                   │
│          masks = out                                                         │
│      masks_np = np.asarray(masks)                                            │
│      if masks_np.ndim == 3:                                                  │
│          mask = masks_np[0].astype(bool)                                     │
│      elif masks_np.ndim == 2:                                                │
│          mask = masks_np.astype(bool)                                        │
│      else:                                                                   │
│          raise RuntimeError(&#x27;Unexpected mask shape from                 │
│  predictor.predict with xywh&#x27;)                                          │
│      return mask                                                             │
│  except Exception:                                                           │
│      pass                                                                    │
│                                                                              │
│  # 4) Some predictors may provide a mask_generator or forward method         │
│  try:                                                                        │
│      if hasattr(predictor, &#x27;mask_generator&#x27;):                      │
│          mg = predictor.mask_generator                                       │
│          # try calling with box                                              │
│          out = mg.generate(image=image_np, box=box)                          │
│          masks_np = np.asarray(out)                                          │
│          if masks_np.ndim == 3:                                              │
│              return masks_np[0].astype(bool)                                 │
│  except Exception:                                                           │
│      pass                                                                    │
│                                                                              │
│  raise RuntimeError(&#x27;Could not obtain a mask from the predictor with    │
│  tried signatures.&#x27;)                                                    │

│                                                                              │

│ def build_predictor(weights_path, device='cpu'): """ Attempt multiple        │
│ reasonable ways to construct a MobileSAM predictor. Returns a tuple          │
│ (predictor, set_image_func_exists) where predictor is the predictor object   │
│ and set_image_func_exists is True if predictor.set_image(image) should be    │
│ called before predict. """ # Common pattern: mobile_sam provides a           │
│ SamPredictor and a sam_model_registry Predictor = None sam = None            │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│  # Try direct SamPredictor + sam_model_registry (like original SAM API)      │
│  try:                                                                        │
│      SamPredictor = getattr(mobile_sam, &#x27;SamPredictor&#x27;, None)      │
│      sam_model_registry = getattr(mobile_sam,                                │
│  &#x27;sam_model_registry&#x27;, None)                                       │
│      if SamPredictor is not None and sam_model_registry is not None:         │

│          # registry may be a dict-like or callable; try some common keys     │
│          model = None                                                        │
│          for key in [&#x27;mobile_sam&#x27;, &#x27;MobileSAM&#x27;,          │
│  &#x27;mobile_sam_vit&#x27;, &#x27;vit_mobile&#x27;]:                        │
│              try:                                                            │
│                  model_cls = sam_model_registry.get(key) if                  │
│  hasattr(sam_model_registry, &#x27;get&#x27;) else sam_model_registry[key]   │
│                  if model_cls is not None:                                   │
│                      try:                                                    │
│                          sam = model_cls(checkpoint=weights_path,            │
│  map_location=&#x27;cpu&#x27;)                                               │
│                      except Exception:                                       │
│                          try:                                                │
│                              sam = model_cls(checkpoint=weights_path)        │
│                          except Exception:                                   │
│                              sam = None                                      │
│                      if sam is not None:                                     │
│                          break                                               │
│              except Exception:                                               │
│                  # try next key                                              │
│                  continue                                                    │
│          # fallback: if registry is callable                                 │
│          if sam is None:                                                     │

│              except Exception:                                               │

│              predictor = SamPredictor(sam)                                   │

│  except Exception:                                                           │

│      if MobileSAM is not None and SamPredictor is not None:                  │
│          try:                                                                │
│              # different constructors: MobileSAM(checkpoint=...) or          │
│  MobileSAM(weights=...)                                                      │
│              try:                                                            │
│                  try:                                                        │
│                      sam = MobileSAM(checkpoint=weights_path,                │
│  map_location=&#x27;cpu&#x27;)                                               │
│                  except Exception:                                           │
│                      sam = MobileSAM(checkpoint=weights_path)                │
│              except Exception:                                               │
│                  try:                                                        │
│                      sam = MobileSAM(weights=weights_path,                   │
│  map_location=&#x27;cpu&#x27;)                                               │
│                  except Exception:                                           │
│                      sam = MobileSAM(weights=weights_path)                   │
│              predictor = SamPredictor(sam)                                   │
│              return predictor, True                                          │
│          except Exception:                                                   │
│              pass                                                            │
│  except Exception:                                                           │
│      pass                                                                    │
│                                                                              │
│  # Try a minimal mobile_sam API where mobile_sam.load_model returns a model  │
│  try:                                                                        │
│      load_model = getattr(mobile_sam, &#x27;load_model&#x27;, None)          │

│ def predict_mask_for_box(predictor, image_np, box, set_image_called_flag):   │
│ """ Given a predictor, an HxWx3 RGB numpy image, and a bbox [x1,y1,x2,y2],   │
│ return a boolean mask (HxW) for that box. Tries a few predictor.predict      │
│ signatures. set_image_called_flag indicates whether                          │
│ predictor.set_image(image) should be called. """ # set image once if needed  │
│ if set_image_called_flag: try: predictor.set_image(image_np) except          │
│ Exception as e: # continue, maybe predictor doesn't need set_image pass      │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│  # Try common predict signatures                                             │
│  box_arr = np.array([box], dtype=np.float32)                                 │
│                                                                              │
│  # 1) predictor.predict(box=...)                                             │
│  try:                                                                        │
│      out = predictor.predict(box=box_arr, multimask_output=False)            │
│      # output formats vary: some return (masks, scores, logits)              │
│      if isinstance(out, tuple) and len(out) &gt;= 1:                         │
│          masks = out[0]                                                      │
│      else:                                                                   │
│          masks = out                                                         │
│      # masks could be (N, H, W) or list                                      │
│      masks_np = np.asarray(masks)                                            │
│      if masks_np.ndim == 3:                                                  │
│          mask = masks_np[0].astype(bool)                                     │
│      elif masks_np.ndim == 2:                                                │
│          mask = masks_np.astype(bool)                                        │
│      else:                                                                   │
│          raise RuntimeError(&#x27;Unexpected mask shape from                 │
│  predictor.predict&#x27;)                                                    │
│      return mask                                                             │
│  except Exception:                                                           │
│      pass                                                                    │
│                                                                              │
│  # 2) predictor.predict_boxes or predictor.predict with boxes arg            │
│  try:                                                                        │
│      out = predictor.predict(boxes=box_arr, multimask_output=False)          │
│      if isinstance(out, tuple) and len(out) &gt;= 1:                         │
│          masks = out[0]                                                      │
│      else:                                                                   │
│          masks = out                                                         │
│      masks_np = np.asarray(masks)                                            │
│      if masks_np.ndim == 3:                                                  │
│          mask = masks_np[0].astype(bool)                                     │
│      elif masks_np.ndim == 2:                                                │
│          mask = masks_np.astype(bool)                                        │
│      else:                                                                   │
│          raise RuntimeError(&#x27;Unexpected mask shape from                 │
│  predictor.predict(boxes=...)&#x27;)                                         │
│      return mask                                                             │
│  except Exception:                                                           │
│      pass                                                                    │
│                                                                              │
│  # 3) predictor.predict with box as (x,y,w,h) maybe                          │
│  try:                                                                        │
│      # convert to xywh                                                       │
│      x1,y1,x2,y2 = box                                                       │
│      xywh = np.array([[x1, y1, x2-x1, y2-y1]], dtype=np.float32)             │
│      out = predictor.predict(box=xywh, multimask_output=False)               │
│      if isinstance(out, tuple) and len(out) &gt;= 1:                         │
│          masks = out[0]                                                      │
│      else:                                                                   │
│          masks = out                                                         │
│      masks_np = np.asarray(masks)                                            │
│      if masks_np.ndim == 3:                                                  │
│          mask = masks_np[0].astype(bool)                                     │
│      elif masks_np.ndim == 2:                                                │
│          mask = masks_np.astype(bool)                                        │
│      else:                                                                   │
│          raise RuntimeError(&#x27;Unexpected mask shape from                 │
│  predictor.predict with xywh&#x27;)                                          │
│      return mask                                                             │
│  except Exception:                                                           │
│      pass                                                                    │
│                                                                              │
│  # 4) Some predictors may provide a mask_generator or forward method         │
│  try:                                                                        │
│      if hasattr(predictor, &#x27;mask_generator&#x27;):                      │
│          mg = predictor.mask_generator                                       │
│          # try calling with box                                              │
│          out = mg.generate(image=image_np, box=box)                          │
│          masks_np = np.asarray(out)                                          │
│          if masks_np.ndim == 3:                                              │

│      pass                                                                    │
│                                                                              │

│  tried signatures.&#x27;)                                                    │

│ def parse_coord_list(s): s = str(s).strip() if s == '' or s.lower() ==       │

│  # Iterate rows; process larger bboxes first to reduce fragmentation         │
│  # compute sort key (area)                                                   │
│  def bbox_area(row):                                                         │

│      except Exception:                                                       │

│                                                                              │
│  order = sorted(range(len(df)), key=lambda i: -bbox_area(df.iloc[i]))        │

│       have a mask. Therefore the script does not guarantee one contiguous    │
│       mask per cell in the output.                                           │
│  2 Trade-off between “no overlap” and “one mask per cell” isn’t resolved:    │
│     • The script currently enforces no overlap by strictly preventing reuse  │
│       of assigned pixels by later masks. That can leave later cells with     │
│       zero unassigned pixels and thus empty outputs. The task requires both: │
│       no overlap AND one contiguous mask per cell — the script enforces the  │
│       former but not the latter.                                             │
│  3 I could not empirically validate MobileSAM integration or runtime         │
│    behavior:                                                                 │
│     • This environment lacks mobile_sam and torch, so I could not run the    │
│       script end-to-end to confirm the predicted masks are polylines,        │
│       non-overlapping pixel-wise, and contiguous in practice.                │
│                                                                              │
│ Concrete suggestions to make the solution fully compliant                    │
│                                                                              │
│  • Ensure each cell ends up with a contiguous, non-empty mask while still    │
│    avoiding overlaps. Possible approaches:                                   │
│     1 Repartition overlapping pixels deterministically between overlapping   │
│       cells instead of reserving them for earlier masks. Example techniques: │
│        • Compute all predicted masks (or raw bbox masks), then resolve       │
│          overlaps by assigning overlapping pixels to the closest mask        │
│          centroid or by largest IoU — then extract a single contiguous       │
│          component per cell (e.g., keep the largest connected piece after    │
│          resolving overlaps).                                                │
│     2 Use a mask-growing / watershed / region-assignment method:             │
│        • Start from seed pixels (for each cell seed could be bbox center or  │
│          polygon centroid) that are guaranteed unique (resolve seeds for     │
│          overlapping bboxes deterministically), then grow regions until      │
│          every seed has a contiguous mask and regions remain                 │
│          non-overlapping.                                                    │
│     3 If a mask would become empty after removing assigned pixels, attempt   │
│       to allocate the nearest contiguous unassigned pixels inside its bbox   │
│       (e.g., morphological dilation from an unassigned seed within bbox) to  │
│       form one contiguous region and then mark them assigned — ensuring no   │
│       overlap.                                                               │
│  • Keep avoiding rectangle fallbacks, but replace “emit empty geometry”      │
│    behavior with a deterministic non-overlapping assignment method so every  │
│    row gets a contiguous polyline.                                           │
│  • Add an optional --report flag that verifies and prints after completion:  │
│     • Per-row whether mask is non-empty, contiguous, and non-rectangular.    │
│     • Global check that pairwise mask intersections sum to zero.             │
│  • Explicit CPU enforcement:                                                 │
│     • Ensure model loading calls actually place tensors on CPU (e.g.,        │
│       torch.load(..., map_location='cpu') when necessary) and test with the  │
│       specific MobileSAM release you'll run against.                         │
│                                                                              │
│ What I need / recommend you run next                                         │
│                                                                              │
│  • Run the script in an environment with torch (CPU), mobile_sam             │
│    (ChaoningZhang/MobileSAM), pandas, numpy, opencv-python, Pillow.          │
│  • After run, perform automatic checks:                                      │
│     • Reconstruct binary masks from coords_x/coords_y and assert pairwise    │
│       overlaps are zero.                                                     │
│     • Assert each mask has exactly one connected component and is non-empty. │
│     • Assert no output mask is a plain rectangle (if strictly required).     │
│  • If any rows are empty or fail contiguity, implement one of the assignment │
│    strategies above to ensure every row gets a contiguous, non-overlapping   │
│    polygon.                                                                  │
│                                                                              │
│ Conclusion                                                                   │
│                                                                              │
│  • The submitted script enforces non-overlap but allows empty outputs for    │
│    fully-overlapped cells, so it does not currently satisfy the requirement  │
│    that every cell has one contiguous mask (and all masks be polylines). The │
│    implementation approach is promising, but it needs a deterministic        │
│    pixel-assignment/resolution step so every row yields one contiguous       │
│    non-overlapping polyline in the final CSV.                                │

│ def predict_mask_for_box(predictor, image_np, box, set_image_called_flag):   │
│ """ Given a predictor, an HxWx3 RGB numpy image, and a bbox [x1,y1,x2,y2],   │
│ return a boolean mask (HxW) for that box. Tries a few predictor.predict      │
│ signatures. set_image_called_flag indicates whether                          │
│ predictor.set_image(image) should be called. """ # set image once if needed  │
│ if set_image_called_flag: try: predictor.set_image(image_np) except          │
│ Exception as e: # continue, maybe predictor doesn't need set_image pass      │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│  # Try common predict signatures                                             │
│  box_arr = np.array([box], dtype=np.float32)                                 │
│                                                                              │
│  # 1) predictor.predict(box=...)                                             │
│  try:                                                                        │
│      out = predictor.predict(box=box_arr, multimask_output=False)            │
│      # output formats vary: some return (masks, scores, logits)              │
│      if isinstance(out, tuple) and len(out) &gt;= 1:                         │
│          masks = out[0]                                                      │
│      else:                                                                   │
│          masks = out                                                         │
│      # masks could be (N, H, W) or list                                      │
│      masks_np = np.asarray(masks)                                            │
│      if masks_np.ndim == 3:                                                  │
│          mask = masks_np[0].astype(bool)                                     │
│      elif masks_np.ndim == 2:                                                │
│          mask = masks_np.astype(bool)                                        │
│      else:                                                                   │
│          raise RuntimeError(&#x27;Unexpected mask shape from                 │
│  predictor.predict&#x27;)                                                    │
│      return mask                                                             │
│  except Exception:                                                           │
│      pass                                                                    │
│                                                                              │
│  # 2) predictor.predict_boxes or predictor.predict with boxes arg            │
│  try:                                                                        │
│      out = predictor.predict(boxes=box_arr, multimask_output=False)          │
│      if isinstance(out, tuple) and len(out) &gt;= 1:                         │
│          masks = out[0]                                                      │
│      else:                                                                   │
│          masks = out                                                         │
│      masks_np = np.asarray(masks)                                            │
│      if masks_np.ndim == 3:                                                  │
│          mask = masks_np[0].astype(bool)                                     │
│      elif masks_np.ndim == 2:                                                │
│          mask = masks_np.astype(bool)                                        │
│      else:                                                                   │
│          raise RuntimeError(&#x27;Unexpected mask shape from                 │
│  predictor.predict(boxes=...)&#x27;)                                         │
│      return mask                                                             │
│  except Exception:                                                           │
│      pass                                                                    │
│                                                                              │
│  # 3) predictor.predict with box as (x,y,w,h) maybe                          │
│  try:                                                                        │
│      # convert to xywh                                                       │
│      x1,y1,x2,y2 = box                                                       │
│      xywh = np.array([[x1, y1, x2-x1, y2-y1]], dtype=np.float32)             │
│      out = predictor.predict(box=xywh, multimask_output=False)               │
│      if isinstance(out, tuple) and len(out) &gt;= 1:                         │
│          masks = out[0]                                                      │
│      else:                                                                   │
│          masks = out                                                         │
│      masks_np = np.asarray(masks)                                            │
│      if masks_np.ndim == 3:                                                  │
│          mask = masks_np[0].astype(bool)                                     │
│      elif masks_np.ndim == 2:                                                │
│          mask = masks_np.astype(bool)                                        │
│      else:                                                                   │
│          raise RuntimeError(&#x27;Unexpected mask shape from                 │
│  predictor.predict with xywh&#x27;)                                          │
│      return mask                                                             │
│  except Exception:                                                           │
│      pass                                                                    │
│                                                                              │
│  # 4) Some predictors may provide a mask_generator or forward method         │
│  try:                                                                        │
│      if hasattr(predictor, &#x27;mask_generator&#x27;):                      │
│          mg = predictor.mask_generator                                       │
│          # try calling with box                                              │
│          out = mg.generate(image=image_np, box=box)                          │
│          masks_np = np.asarray(out)                                          │
│          if masks_np.ndim == 3:                                              │
│              return masks_np[0].astype(bool)                                 │
│  except Exception:                                                           │
│      pass                                                                    │
│                                                                              │
│  raise RuntimeError(&#x27;Could not obtain a mask from the predictor with    │
│  tried signatures.&#x27;)                                                    │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│ </output>                                                                    │

│    rectangular contours; if strict prohibition of axis-aligned rectangle     │
│    polygons is required, add a post-filter to detect & re-process            │
│    rectangular outputs (e.g., request more prompt types, points, or run      │
│    multimask output).                                                        │
│  • The script chooses Euclidean nearest-seed assignment to partition         │
│    overlapping pixels. This is deterministic and generally works well, but   │
│    you may prefer other conflict resolution strategies (largest IoU,         │
│    priority by size, watershed with image gradients, etc.). I can switch to  │
│    another strategy if you prefer.                                           │
│  • I could not validate performance or memory use on large images here;      │
│    ensure to test on representative hidden-test images.                      │
│  • The script will emit empty coords for a row only if no pixels in          │
│    union_domain are assigned to that row. This should be rare because        │
│    union_domain is union of bboxes; but if a bbox has zero area or is        │
│    outside the image, the row may be empty.                                  │
│                                                                              │
│ How to run (in your environment)                                             │
│                                                                              │
│  1 Ensure dependencies are installed (CPU builds):                           │
│     • torch (CPU), torchvision                                               │
│     • mobile_sam (ChaoningZhang/MobileSAM distilled model)                   │
│     • numpy, pandas, opencv-python, Pillow, tqdm                             │
│  2 Run: python /app/convert_masks.py --weights_path                          │
│    /path/to/mobilesam_weights.pt                                             │
│    --output_path /path/to/output_dir                                         │
│    --rgb_path /path/to/image.png                                             │
│    --csv_path /path/to/metadata.csv                                          │
│  3 Output:                                                                   │
│     • The script writes an updated CSV to output_path with the same filename │
│       as the input CSV and updated xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax, coords_x,         │
│       coords_y fields.                                                       │
│                                                                              │
│ Post-run verification (recommended)                                          │
│                                                                              │
│  • Reconstruct binary masks from coords_x/coords_y for all rows (skip rows   │
│    with empty coords) and:                                                   │
│     • Assert that for any pair of masks their intersection is empty (no      │
│       pixel overlap).                                                        │
│     • Assert each mask has exactly one connected component (contiguity).     │
│     • Check that coords_x/coords_y are not simply 4-point bbox corners (if   │
│       strictly disallowing rectangles).                                      │
│  • If any cell ends up empty, examine its bbox and predictions to decide     │
│    whether to:                                                               │
│     • Accept empties (if cell fully overlapped by stronger neighbors), or    │
│     • Use a different assignment strategy (give some pixels back to that     │
│       cell using proximity inside bbox), or                                  │
│     • Re-run MobileSAM for that cell with alternate prompts (center point +  │
│       bbox).                                                                 │
│                                                                              │
│ If you want next                                                             │
│                                                                              │
│  • I can:                                                                    │
│     • Add a --report flag to the script that runs the three verification     │
│       checks automatically after writing output and prints a summary (counts │
│       of empty outputs, overlaps, contiguity failures, rectangle-like        │
│       masks).                                                                │
│     • Implement alternative conflict resolution strategies (IoU-based,       │
│       watershed) if you prefer them over nearest-seed assignment.            │
│     • Add additional MobileSAM prompt strategies for stubborn/empty cases    │
│       (e.g., re-prompt using the cell bbox center or multimask outputs).     │
│     • Run the script end-to-end if you provide an environment or confirm the │
│       packages are available.                                                │
│                                                                              │
│ Final note                                                                   │
│                                                                              │
│  • The script implemented a deterministic non-overlapping assignment and     │
│    attempts to produce one contiguous (non-overlapping) mask per cell.       │
│    Empirical validation requires running in an environment with mobile_sam   │
│    and torch installed — please run the script there and let me know the     │
│    verification results; I will iterate further as needed.                   │

│ def build_predictor(weights_path, device='cpu'): """ Attempt multiple        │
│ reasonable ways to construct a MobileSAM predictor. Returns a tuple          │

│ SamPredictor and a sam_model_registry Predictor = None sam = None            │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│  # Try direct SamPredictor + sam_model_registry (like original SAM API)      │
│  try:                                                                        │
│      SamPredictor = getattr(mobile_sam, &#x27;SamPredictor&#x27;, None)      │
│      sam_model_registry = getattr(mobile_sam,                                │
│  &#x27;sam_model_registry&#x27;, None)                                       │

│              try:                                                            │
│                  model_cls = sam_model_registry.get(key) if                  │
│  hasattr(sam_model_registry, &#x27;get&#x27;) else sam_model_registry[key]   │
│                  if model_cls is not None:                                   │
│                      try:                                                    │

│  map_location=&#x27;cpu&#x27;)                                               │
│                      except Exception:                                       │
│                          try:                                                │
│                              sam = model_cls(checkpoint=weights_path)        │
│                          except Exception:                                   │
│                              sam = None                                      │
│                      if sam is not None:                                     │
│                          break                                               │
│              except Exception:                                               │
│                  # try next key                                              │
│                  continue                                                    │
│          # fallback: if registry is callable                                 │

│              # different constructors: MobileSAM(checkpoint=...) or          │

│          except Exception:                                                   │
│              pass                                                            │

│ def predict_mask_for_box(predictor, image_np, box, set_image_called_flag):   │
│ """ Given a predictor, an HxWx3 RGB numpy image, and a bbox [x1,y1,x2,y2],   │
│ return a boolean mask (HxW) for that box. Tries a few predictor.predict      │
│ signatures. set_image_called_flag indicates whether                          │
│ predictor.set_image(image) should be called. """ # set image once if needed  │
│ if set_image_called_flag: try: predictor.set_image(image_np) except          │
│ Exception as e: # continue, maybe predictor doesn't need set_image pass      │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│  # Try common predict signatures                                             │
│  box_arr = np.array([box], dtype=np.float32)                                 │
│                                                                              │
│  # 1) predictor.predict(box=...)                                             │
│  try:                                                                        │
│      out = predictor.predict(box=box_arr, multimask_output=False)            │
│      # output formats vary: some return (masks, scores, logits)              │
│      if isinstance(out, tuple) and len(out) &gt;= 1:                         │
│          masks = out[0]                                                      │
│      else:                                                                   │
│          masks = out                                                         │
│      # masks could be (N, H, W) or list                                      │
│      masks_np = np.asarray(masks)                                            │
│      if masks_np.ndim == 3:                                                  │
│          mask = masks_np[0].astype(bool)                                     │
│      elif masks_np.ndim == 2:                                                │
│          mask = masks_np.astype(bool)                                        │
│      else:                                                                   │
│          raise RuntimeError(&#x27;Unexpected mask shape from                 │
│  predictor.predict&#x27;)                                                    │
│      return mask                                                             │
│  except Exception:                                                           │
│      pass                                                                    │
│                                                                              │
│  # 2) predictor.predict_boxes or predictor.predict with boxes arg            │
│  try:                                                                        │
│      out = predictor.predict(boxes=box_arr, multimask_output=False)          │
│      if isinstance(out, tuple) and len(out) &gt;= 1:                         │
│          masks = out[0]                                                      │
│      else:                                                                   │
│          masks = out                                                         │
│      masks_np = np.asarray(masks)                                            │
│      if masks_np.ndim == 3:                                                  │
│          mask = masks_np[0].astype(bool)                                     │
│      elif masks_np.ndim == 2:                                                │
│          mask = masks_np.astype(bool)                                        │
│      else:                                                                   │
│          raise RuntimeError(&#x27;Unexpected mask shape from                 │
│  predictor.predict(boxes=...)&#x27;)                                         │
│      return mask                                                             │
│  except Exception:                                                           │
│      pass                                                                    │
│                                                                              │
│  # 3) predictor.predict with box as (x,y,w,h) maybe                          │
│  try:                                                                        │
│      # convert to xywh                                                       │
│      x1,y1,x2,y2 = box                                                       │
│      xywh = np.array([[x1, y1, x2-x1, y2-y1]], dtype=np.float32)             │
│      out = predictor.predict(box=xywh, multimask_output=False)               │
│      if isinstance(out, tuple) and len(out) &gt;= 1:                         │
│          masks = out[0]                                                      │
│      else:                                                                   │
│          masks = out                                                         │
│      masks_np = np.asarray(masks)                                            │
│      if masks_np.ndim == 3:                                                  │
│          mask = masks_np[0].astype(bool)                                     │
│      elif masks_np.ndim == 2:                                                │
│          mask = masks_np.astype(bool)                                        │
│      else:                                                                   │

│    masks in the provided CSV into non-overlapping, contiguous polylines      │
│    using MobileSAM (distilled MobileSAM).                                    │
│  • Key features:                                                             │
│     • Accepts argparse args: --weights_path, --output_path, --rgb_path,      │
│       --csv_path.                                                            │
│     • Robust MobileSAM loader attempts (multiple common mobile_sam APIs) and │
│       attempts to load weights on CPU (map_location='cpu' where supported).  │
│     • Predicts a mask for each cell using its bounding box as a prompt.      │
│     • Resolves overlaps deterministically by:                                │
│        • Collecting all predicted masks and bboxes,                          │
│        • Creating a union domain of all bbox pixels,                         │
│        • Creating one seed per cell (centroid of its largest predicted       │
│          component or bbox center),                                          │
│        • Assigning each pixel in the union domain to the nearest seed        │
│          (Euclidean distance) to partition pixels disjointly,                │
│        • Iteratively reassigning small islands so each cell's assigned       │
│          pixels form a single contiguous connected component.                │
│     • Extracts a simplified polygon (polyline) per cell from the contiguous  │
│       assigned region, ensures closed polygons, updates xmin/ymin/xmax/ymax  │
│       and coords_x/coords_y in the output CSV.                               │
│     • Avoids writing rectangle fallback polygons; instead uses partitioning  │
│       to guarantee each assigned cell has a disjoint contiguous mask derived │
│       from predictions and bboxes. If a label has zero assigned pixels       │
│       (rare), the script emits empty coords for that row rather than         │
│       inventing overlap-creating geometry.                                   │
│     • Writes updated CSV with same filename into output_path, with coords    │
│       written as comma-separated integer lists (quoted to match input        │
│       style).                                                                │
│                                                                              │

│    logic through the mocked runs.                                            │
